text:
anya: Heads up — noticed a small but steady canary drift in rollout/2026-03-canary (5% target) where ~0.6% of traffic keeps getting routed back to Stable after initial sticky assignment. Increasingly visible in the last 3 hours.

mike: repro steps? any specific client attrs?

anya: steps: hit /generate with header X-Experiment: blue, cookie set rdw_bucket=canary; expect repeated requests same bucket. But we see logs where first request -> canary, subsequent requests -> stable. Log snippet:```2026-03-18T12:03:22Z cid=abc123 route=canary set_cookie=rdw_bucket=canary; 2026-03-18T12:03:23Z cid=abc123 route=stable cookie=rdw_bucket=canary```

olivia: hmm that looks like cookie TTL/eviction or our routing guard picking fallback. Telemetry shows a tiny spike in "route_fallback" counter matching timestamps. I also see the header normalization metric tick up at the same time window.

luis: did anything change in the edge proxy / header handling recently? case-sensitivity or header dedupe?

infra-bot: deploybot: deploy 2245801000 to edge-proxy succeeded (image: proxy:v2.14.0) at 2245801005

mike: proxy v2.14 had a change to preserve raw header case for debugging (we reverted normalization). Could that break our header-based rollout guard which expects lowercase keys? If the guard checks for "x-experiment" but proxy now exposes "X-Experiment" it might not match and fall back to hashing policy.

anya: interesting — but the cookie should still ensure stickiness. Why would cookie not keep it on canary?

luis: two possibilities: 1) cookie path/ttl attributes not set when response comes from canary (edge strip), 2) our session affinity logic uses header precedence over cookie when header present but unrecognized, and that code path was changed last week.

olivia: pulled telemetry by client id. 98% of affected clients are IPv6; also many are mobile carriers. Could be CDN edge returning slightly different header casing.

mike: quick diagnostic patch: normalize headers before routing and prefer existing cookie bucket if present. I can push a hotfix to runtime routing layer (non-proxy) in 10m.

luis: do we have a safe toggle in Console to force cookie-first stickiness for this rollout? Would be quicker than a code deploy.

anya: Console has a "stickiness precedence" toggle but it's a per-rollout flag and current canary was created with "header_priority" enabled. I can flip it but need approval (safety shield).

mike: go ahead, flip it for canary/2026-03 and also add a short-lived alert on route_fallback > 0.2% for next 12h. I'll ship the normalize-headers patch right after.

deploy-bot: config-change 2245804310 by anya: rollout/canary/2026-03 stickiness_precedence=COOKIE -> applied

anya: flipped. Monitoring: route_fallback dropped from 0.62% -> 0.05% within 6 mins.

olivia: great signal. mike, please still land header-normalize — it prevents future regressions and odd CDN behavior. Also add unit test for mixed-case headers in routing rules.

mike: will do. Plan: (1) routing-layer normalize headers before policy eval (2) prefer cookie bucket if cookie present (3) add test + small telemetry for header-case-mismatch. Target deploy in next patch window (in 2 hours).

luis: can we also add a Console warning when someone creates a header-based rollout reminding them about header casing and CDN behavior? Small UX nudge.

anya: good idea. I'll file a tiny product ticket and pin to rollout page.

mike: thanks all. follow-up: I'll post PR link and post-deploy telemetry in this thread. :thumbsup:
